data.name: The Last Time
data.detailed_description:
The Last Time combines retro graphics and point-and-click game mechanics with innovative, nonlinear storytelling.

You play as Jack Glover, a retired police officer, who has withdrawn from society – until a mysterious phone call starts a series of events which forces him back into the real world.

Now, Jack must overcome some new challenges - his physical frailty, his ignorance of modern technology, and his fear of connecting with people - if he's going to finally conquer his demons.

Features

  • Nonlinear, emotional story
  • Puzzles with multiple solutions
  • Original soundtrack
  • Branching dialogue trees
  • Dynamic action sequences
  • Dark humour

data.short_description: The Last Time features the narrative depth and emotional impact of a modern adventure title, delivered with the graphical style and game mechanics of a classic point-and-click. Play as Jack Glover, a frail old man who must come out of retirement to face his demons.

reviews.review:
BottomLine at the Top:  Although lacking in any real inventory interactions and thus barely qualifying as a "true" point and click adventure, this game's story and dramatic music scoring really pull you into it.  


-------------------------------------
Pros
-------------------------------------
-The Game Informer review states that this game "evokes Quantic Dream and Telltale Games in spades" and I strongly agree.  Those studio's titles (The Walking Dead series and Heavy Rain for example) primary focus is more on storytelling than in depth interactive game play and it's very much the case for The Last Time as well.
-This is the second retro pixel game I've played (the first being The Last Door by developer The Game Kitchen) that made use of strong music cues and well-timed sound effects to invoke emotion.  It’s a cool "mechanic" that works well.  I think both games show how effective and important a good sound design can be in telling a story. 


-------------------------------------
Meh.
-------------------------------------
-There is no voice acting however the style of the game is such that it ends up working better without it.  
-No Steam achievements.
-Almost no inventory interactions.  This is a pretty strong fundamental part of what I consider "true" point and click games and the lack of them here puts it much more in the realm of a "choices matter" type game.  Still, I would not consider it an interactive novel as the overarching style of the game does end up feeling very P&C.
-I thought there were no saves but it’s just that the save locations are inconsistent and not always available.


-------------------------------------
Cons
-------------------------------------
-At 2.5 hours of game play it's short.  The story could have built in another act or two and it would have made the ending more powerful.


At the regular asking price of $4, I'd recommend waiting for a sale.  It's got a good story but it’s not super engrossing (nor has a long amount of) game play.  Overall, I enjoyed it and I'd like to see what else this developer comes up with in the future!
